Recently, I visited this diagnostic centre in Thakur Village, Kandivali East, and had a very bitter experience. I would like to highlight a few issues. Firstly, although the centre is located in Thakur Village, they have provided the contact number of their Goregaon branch on the website, which is misleading.

My physician had advised me to get a USG test of the whole abdomen and pelvis. For this test, one must remain on an empty stomach for at least 6–7 hours. However, the staff at this centre seem extremely money-minded, as they conduct sonography even if the patient is not fasting for this test. Though I had kept my stomach empty, but I was surprised to see that even people who had barely drunk water were being taken in for sonography.

They appear more focused on making money through corporate tie-ups and even offer a ₹50 cashback for giving feedback.

When I met the radiologist, Dr. Foram Ajmera, she only asked me about the type of pain I was experiencing and performed a partial sonography based on that, despite my prescription clearly mentioning a full USG of the whole abdomen and pelvis. I paid ₹1,600 for the test, yet she did not examine the left side of my abdomen, nor did she perform the pelvic scan. Though she explained me very well the symptoms she observed on the right side.

After receiving the report, I was not satisfied and consulted her again. She gave vague explanations, saying that since I mentioned pain on the right side, she only checked that area. Later, she asked me to come again for the pelvic scan, which she had skipped earlier. She checked the pelvic area in barely 30 seconds and then argued that everything was normal.
She further stated that if I could show her my previous reports, she would compare them and check whether the earlier issues still existed—something she should have done during the initial test itself . My POV is if you examine properly during sonography you don't have to compare or rely on previous reports

My main concern is that despite charging such high fees, patients are not being examined properly. Completing a sonography in just 2 minutes is quite risky and raises serious doubts about the accuracy and quality of the diagnosis.
